paper.central_claim: Existing self-evolving prompt frameworks (GEPA, ACE, MemEvolve) degrade on heterogeneous task distributions; CluE, a cluster-based self-evolving strategy that clusters training examples by extraction scenario, analyzes each cluster independently and synthesizes cross-cluster insights, evolves a memory-extraction prompt that generalizes across heterogeneous tasks (+9.04% relative gain on BEHEMOTH) and consistently outperforms prior frameworks.
paper.title: Self-Evolving LLM Memory Extraction Across Heterogeneous Tasks

evidence.quote: existing self-evolving prompt optimization frameworks, originally designed for homogeneous distributions, degrade when training tasks are heterogeneous.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prior prompt-evolution loops assume homogeneous tasks.

evidence.quote: Updating prompts too frequently risks overfitting to recent examples, while updating too infrequently slows adaptation and dilutes feedback signals across dissimilar examples.
evidence.support_explanation: States the instability/dilution dilemma that CluE targets.

evidence.quote: training examples are grouped into clusters that share similar memory extraction scenarios, and analysis is performed per cluster rather than over the entire batch.
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation of CluE.

evidence.quote: It identifies general principles shared across clusters, organizes cluster-specific insights into structured guidelines, and resolves conflicting recommendations by scoping them to relevant memory categories.
evidence.support_explanation: Proposer step: how per-cluster analyses are merged into a prompt edit and conflicts handled.

evidence.quote: we hold out one dataset per category
evidence.support_explanation: OOD held-out datasets (LongMemEval, GPQA-Diamond, ToolBench) not used in evolution.

evidence.quote: we randomly sample 20 examples from each (50 for AIME, which aggregates multiple competition years) to form the training set (330 in total, randomly shuffled) and use the rest as in-distribution test sets.
evidence.support_explanation: Train/test split inside each in-distribution dataset: evolution on 330 examples, tests are the disjoint remainder.

evidence.quote: Our method yields the highest overall relative gain
evidence.support_explanation: CluE +9.04% overall vs GEPA +5.06, ACE +3.56, MemEvolve +2.11 relative to the Simple seed (Table 2).

evidence.quote: gains on some categories come at the cost of regressions on others.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline category trade-offs (GEPA -2.16 personalization, MemEvolve -3.25 agentic) that motivate the claim.
OOD results: LongMemEval 63.07, GPQA-D 48.48±1.80, ToolBench 26.67.
Nearest baseline OOD: GPQA-D 47.98±1.09 (overlaps CluE) and ToolBench identical 26.67.

evidence.quote: does not drop below the Simple prompt on GPQA-Diamond or ToolBench
evidence.support_explanation: OOD claim; but no gain over MemEvolve there.

evidence.quote: GEPA fails to find any improvement and returns the seed unchanged.
evidence.support_explanation: Stronger-seed (Survey) experiment: baselines fail or regress, CluE +6.54%.

evidence.quote: On the Agentic category, all evolved prompts, including ours, fall below the Simple baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: With a Gemini-3-Flash backend CluE regresses on agentic (-5.93%) although overall +3.40%; contradicts 'consistent' improvement.

evidence.quote: introducing moderate optimizer overhead (221 vs. 30 calls) at a marginal wall-time cost
evidence.support_explanation: Cost accounting: CluE 221 optimization calls vs MemEvolve 30; wall time ~5.5h vs ~5.0h; eval calls 1,150 each.

evidence.quote: Our CluE adopts the exact same hyperparameters as MemEvolve.
evidence.support_explanation: CluE inherits MemEvolve's round/batch/tournament settings (5 rounds, batch 35 + 10).

evidence.quote: and the winner advances to the next round.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection/retention rule: tournament among seed + 3 candidates on fresh examples; winner becomes incumbent.

evidence.quote: We isolate memory extraction from orthogonal factors such as memory retrieval and management
evidence.support_explanation: Single-step protocol: retrieval/consolidation excluded from the main evaluation.

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise stated, we use Qwen3-32B as both the generation model and the extraction model throughout all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Single model family for extraction, generation and (per App A.2) optimization.

evidence.quote: Subscripts denote standard deviations over three runs.
evidence.support_explanation: Std is over three repeats of the evaluation pipeline (App A.1), not over independent evolution runs.

evidence.quote: We select two tasks on which CluE outperforms MemEvolve in the single-step evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: Continual-setting check uses tasks selected where CluE already wins: selection by results.

evidence.quote: yet our prompts are evolved exclusively under the single-step regime where source conversations are memory-free.
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt never evolved/tested in a closed retain-retrieve-reuse loop; only a post-hoc continual check.

evidence.quote: No single static memory extraction prompt dominates.
evidence.support_explanation: Empirical characterization of heterogeneity (Table 1).

evidence.quote: evolves per-domain memory skill banks using a PPO-trained controller with hard-case clustering.
evidence.support_explanation: MemSkill uses hard-case clustering: a close neighbor that is described but not compared experimentally.

evidence.quote: The resulting prompt (1,403 tokens) is considerably longer than those of GEPA (1,243), CluE (936), and MemEvolve (539)
evidence.support_explanation: Evolved prompt lengths differ by up to ~2x; prompt length is an uncontrolled alternative explanation.

evidence.quote: we reserve 100 examples from the training set as a validation set and optimize over the remaining 230 examples.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines use different data usage than CluE/MemEvolve (ACE online, no validation) i.e. re-implemented baselines with differing protocols.

evidence.quote: LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2025) – 176 LLM Judge
evidence.support_explanation: The largest OOD gain (LongMemEval) is scored by an LLM judge; other datasets use rule/accuracy.

evidence.quote: we adopt a utility-driven metric rather than LLM-based judges
evidence.support_explanation: Primary metric is downstream utility of the extracted memory.

evidence.quote: The cluster pool starts with 7 fine-grained clusters and consolidates over rounds
evidence.support_explanation: Optimizer-internal state (cluster pool) persists and is merged/split across rounds.

evidence.quote: All code and data have been publicly available at
evidence.support_explanation: Code and data release claimed (not inspected).

evidence.quote: MemEvolve lacks a memory taxonomy and instead introduces a penalty clause that prohibits specific extraction patterns.
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative evidence that the evolved prompt structure differs; author interpretation of why gaps arise.

gap.author_gap: Static extraction rules are tailored to narrow contexts and no benchmark evaluates memory extraction across heterogeneous tasks; existing self-evolving frameworks assume homogeneous distributions.
gap.checked_gap: Supported empirically: no static prompt dominates (Table 1) and each baseline trades categories (Table 2). The 'designed for homogeneous' premise is asserted; no experiment shows the baselines succeed on homogeneous splits.
gap.lineage: APE/OPRO -> GEPA/ACE (prompt/playbook evolution) -> MemEvolve (analyzer-proposer tournament) -> CluE (adds scenario clustering and per-cluster analysis); memory side: Mem0/ReasoningBank/Dynamic Cheatsheet fixed extraction -> learnable extraction prompt.
gap.closest_adjacent: MemEvolve (same architecture/hyperparameters; compared) and MemSkill (hard-case clustering per domain with PPO controller; described but not compared), ALMA and Evo-Memory (described).
gap.residue: Dilution vs instability when updating a single prompt from dissimilar examples.
gap.stakes: Baselines regress on some categories (GEPA personalization -2.16, MemEvolve agentic -3.25) and degrade a stronger seed (ACE -1.44, MemEvolve -0.74).
gap.method_response: Group by extraction scenario, analyze per cluster, then synthesize a prompt that scopes conflicting advice.
gap.remaining_gap: Continual/closed-loop regime, storage/retrieval/management stages, backend where headroom is small (Gemini agentic).
unresolved: Whether MemSkill-style clustering baseline would match CluE

G.reason: Concrete fixed object (extraction prompt) and a measured residual: Table 1 and Table 2 show no static prompt dominates and baselines trade categories; neighbors enumerated, but the closest clustering neighbor (MemSkill) is not compared and the 'baselines assume homogeneity' premise is asserted.

M.reason: Chain from logs to scenario summaries to clusters to per-cluster analysis to a scoped prompt edit addresses the stated dilution/instability dilemma and yields distinguishable qualitative predictions (Fig. 4 taxonomy vs recency bias); the causal role of clustering vs added analysis calls is not isolated.

X.reason: Steps, hyperparameters (inherits MemEvolve's), selection tournament and persistent cluster pool are described and code is released; rollback/versioning of the retained prompt is not described and prompt figures were not in the text material.

E.measurement.reason: Downstream-utility metric with mostly rule/accuracy rewards and a No-Memory floor; weaknesses are the single Qwen3-32B for all roles, LLM-judged LongMemEval/ToolBench, and LLM-completed source conversations.

E.causality.reason: Same-seed, same-model comparison with three optimizers and extra seed/backend settings, but no component ablation, 7x optimizer calls vs MemEvolve, prompt length uncontrolled (936 vs 539 tokens) and baselines re-implemented with different data protocols.

E.holdout.reason: Evolution on 330 training examples, tests on disjoint remainder, plus three held-out datasets; deduction because OOD advantage appears only on LLM-judged LongMemEval and the continual check used tasks selected where CluE already won.

E.statistics.reason: Std over three evaluation repeats for small test sets and negative/regression results are shown, but there is no variance across independent evolution runs, no significance test, and OOD differences overlap within std.

E.cost.reason: Wall time, optimization LLM calls and evaluation calls are reported for all four optimizers, including CluE's 221 vs 30 call overhead; budget is disclosed but not matched and token costs are absent.
